maya: Heads-up — since the 2026-03-15 deploy we're seeing 99th percentile latency spikes on hosted endpoints. nsys traces show multiple cudaMalloc bursts right at batch boundaries.

tomas: Which endpoint/pool? sounds like kernel-selector changes landed last night. any perfetto/nsys links?

maya: Impacting chat-v2-redwood-small on the dedicated prod pool. Pattern: stable latency at batch_size≈8 then big spikes when batches jump to 24–32. Logs show repeated 'kv_cache: evict slab' messages around the same time. Example log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T03:21:12Z] kv_cache: evict slab id=42 size=128K reason=pressure
[2026-03-15T03:21:12Z] runtime: cudamalloc fallback slow-path 128K alloc
[2026-03-15T03:21:12Z] batcher: batch formed size=28 sd=6
```

alex: I uploaded an nsys profile + perfetto timeline: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abc123 (nsys output: trace-1849991111.qdrep). Command used: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt -o trace-1849991111 --force-overwrite --capture-range=cuda_api`

alex: TL;DR from the trace: kernel-selector picked the "long-seq" kernel for ~20% of requests that actually had short KV hits. The long-seq path allocates ~1MB scratch then falls back to cudaMalloc for a bunch of small device buffers (~64–256KB) due to arena fragmentation. Those cudaMalloc calls show up as 100–200ms gaps in the timeline.

perf-bot: deploy: rollout/2026-03-15-03:12 by tomas to dedicated-prod (canary 10%) :rocket: — linked trace auto-ingested (trace id abc123).

olga: Sounds like two problems colliding: (1) kernel misrouting when batch-length distribution is multi-modal, (2) small-allocation churn hitting the pool slow path. Quick experiments I'd try: bump arena chunk size, increase slab granularity, and add a soft heuristic to kernel-selector to prefer compact-workspace kernels when batch_length_stddev > 5. Example pool config we tried in staging: 
```
{"gpu_mem_pool": {"arena_chunk_size": "1MB", "min_slab": "1MB", "max_slab": "8MB", "slab_alignment": "64B", "alloc_retry": 2}}
```

olga: Also enable the alloc sampler for a 10m run: `python -m rwinf.tools.alloc_sampler --pid <pid> --duration 600 --out alloc-184999.csv` — that'll show distribution of sizes hitting cudamalloc.

maya: Ran alloc_sampler for 15m. Results: ~65% of device allocs during spikes are 64–256KB, median 128KB, ~1.6k allocations/sec peak. After applying arena_chunk_size=1MB and increasing slab to 1MB we saw the number of cudaMalloc calls drop ~5x in a quick canary.

tomas: Nice. Can you also paste a small nvtx timeline snapshot? looking for back-to-back allocs inside the batcher NVTX range.

maya: nvtx snippet from perfetto: 
```
NVTX[batch_start:id=100] -> kernel_dispatch(short_seq) -> kernel_dispatch(long_seq) -> device_mem_alloc(128KB) x6 -> kv_cache:evict -> cudamalloc fallback
```

alex: Suggest adding a tiny kernel-selector rule: if predicted_batch_length_stddev > 4 and p(kv_hit) > 0.6 then prefer compact-kernel variant. Pseudocode: 
```
if batcher.stddev(len(batch)) > THRESH and kv_cache.hit_rate(batch) > 0.6:
  select_kernel(compact_workspace)
else:
  select_kernel(low_compute)
```

maya: After applying arena and selector tweak to canary (10% traffic) for 1h: 99th latency for that endpoint dropped 72%, cudaMalloc events reduced ~80% in the trace. We'll schedule a staged rollout + a longer 6h perf-run tomorrow.

tomas: Great. Can you open a small RFC PR with the config diff and add the alloc_sampler command to the perf checklist? I want the SRE runbook updated to include: how-to collect alloc_sampler, nsys flags we used, and sample perfetto link.

maya: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
